findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - the full suite runs on a loaded GitHub worker.
Splitting the scenarios removes the final merge from this invocation, but the human-merge case still has two sequential 60-second waits, plus `fix start`, the simulated merge, and `forge next`. The simulated merge runs six Git commands with individual 60-second limits (`tests/test_runner_moves_approved_work_to_merge.py:330`), and each Forge command also has a 60-second limit (`tests/conftest.py:346`), while `forge.toml:6` limits the whole test to 150 seconds. If the commands take 41 seconds in total and the two waits take 55 seconds each, pytest terminates the test even though every individual operation is within its limit. The test can therefore still fail on a loaded machine.
